transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I, um... I hope I'm not overreacting or wasting your time, but I finally decided to call the employee assistance program at work. 

It's mostly just... well, I'm barely sleeping right lately. I'm sure it's just normal stress, but I just lie there in bed kind of replaying things from the office, or... you know, little arguments from home. Nothing major, just typical stuff, I promise. But I keep waking up around 3 or 4 in the morning, and then when I have to actually start my day, I feel like I never really rested at all. 

Is that... does that sound like the right kind of thing to come here for?
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about everyday things?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I think about work, obviously... being a manager, you have to stay on top of things and make sure the team is hitting their numbers. But I wouldn't call it excessive worrying. Just the normal amount of, you know, being responsible? 

I really try to keep a positive attitude and not let things get to me during the day. I hope that's a good thing? It's really just at night, when it's quiet, that my brain kind of gets stuck on those little things I mentioned. But during the day, I feel like I handle everyday stuff just fine. Does that make sense?
Have you experienced any traumatic events recently?

No, no, nothing like that. I've been very lucky, really. No big traumas or anything terrible happening. Life is... it's pretty stable, actually. My wife and I get along fine, work is steady. I know some people go through awful things, and I definitely haven't had to deal with anything on that level. I hope it's okay that I don't have a clear reason for why I'm not sleeping well? I almost feel guilty being here when everything is technically fine.
Do you feel tired or fatigued during the day?

Well, um, maybe a little? But I think that's just because of the sleep thing, you know? It's not like I'm falling asleep at my desk or anything like that. I still get all my work done and make sure my team is supported. 

I might just need an extra cup of coffee in the afternoon, which I think is pretty standard for most people, right? I really try to push through it so it doesn't affect my performance or, you know, bother anyone else. I just don't want you to think I'm slacking off or anything. It's just a normal kind of tired, I'm pretty sure. Is that... is that what you meant?
Do you have trouble concentrating?

Well... maybe a little bit? I mean, I'm definitely still getting all my work done, I don't want you to think I'm dropping the ball or anything. 

It's just... I guess I used to be able to knock out my sales forecasts and client decks pretty quickly. But lately, I'll catch myself reading the same slide like five times. And I end up second-guessing every number, or I just sit there and can't quite decide what to say. 

I think I'm just being extra thorough, maybe? Or just wanting to get it exactly right for the clients. I really hope that doesn't make me sound incompetent. I'm still doing a good job, it just takes a bit more effort right now. Is it normal to get a little bogged down like that sometimes?
Are there things you used to enjoy doing but have stopped doing recently?

Um, well, I still try to make time for things, I really do. I don't want to be a flake or let my buddies down. But... I guess maybe a little bit? 

I used to always look forward to things like our pickup basketball games, or bowling nights. Even bigger stuff, like going to music festivals or just firing up the smoker in the backyard for everyone. But lately... I don't know, I find myself canceling more often than I used to. And even when I do show up, I kind of feel like I'm just going through the motions. 

I mean, I still love hanging out with everyone! I don't want you to think I'm isolating myself or anything like that. I just... maybe I'm just getting a bit older and need more quiet time on the weekends? That's pretty normal for guys my age, right? I just hope I'm not being a bad friend by staying in a little more.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain social situations or activities because you feel anxious or uncomfortable?

Oh, no, definitely not. Um, I don't really get anxious around people at all. I mean, being in sales, you kind of have to be a people person, right? I'm totally comfortable in a room full of strangers or pitching to big clients. 

I really wouldn't want you to think I'm, you know, hiding out because I'm scared or awkward or anything like that. If I'm staying in on a Friday, it's really just that energy thing I mentioned earlier, not because I'm uncomfortable. I'm still a very outgoing guy, I promise. I hope that makes sense?
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?

Um... well, I really wouldn't want you to think I'm sitting around crying all day or anything like that. I'm definitely still keeping a positive face on for the team. But... I guess if I'm being completely honest, yeah, maybe a little down. 

Most days it just feels like there's this... this heavy, kind of gray mood that just follows me around. Like, from the office, into the car, and then into the house. And it's weird because nothing specific is even happening to make me upset, you know? I just feel kind of... hollow. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound ungrateful. I have a great life, a good job, I know I do. I think it's probably just a bit of a funk, right? Lots of guys go through phases like this, don't they? I just want to make sure I'm not overreacting.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um... wow, when I really think about it... I guess it's been a little while. Maybe about a year and two months? 

I, uh... I feel a little bad even mentioning this, because I really don't want to paint a bad picture of my home life. I'm incredibly lucky, I really am. But... I suppose it started right around the time the arguments at home started getting a lot worse. 

Just... you know, disagreements. I'm sure every relationship goes through rough patches where you bicker a bit more, right? I just... I guess I let the stress of it get to me a little more than I should have. That's completely understandable, isn't it? I just really don't want to sound like I'm making excuses or blaming anyone else for my mood.
Do you find that you're no longer enjoying things that you used to find pleasurable?

Um... well, I wouldn't say I've completely stopped enjoying things. I really don't want you to think I'm just sitting around the house doing absolutely nothing. I'm still trying to stay active, I really am. 

But... I guess, if I'm being totally honest... things just don't have the same spark they used to? Like, I used to always look forward to playing pickup basketball, or going to bowling nights with the guys. And I loved going to music festivals, or just firing up the smoker in the backyard and having friends over. 

Lately, though... I don't know. A lot of times I just end up canceling. Or if I do go, I'm kind of just... going through the motions, you know? It's not that I don't like my friends or those activities anymore, I promise. It's just... I guess I just haven't been as into it lately. That's pretty normal when you're stressed out, right? I'm sure I'll bounce back and get back into the swing of things soon.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

Um... well, actually, no, I haven't lost weight. I really don't want to sound like I'm not taking care of myself, because I try to eat healthy when I can. But... if anything, I think I've actually gained a little bit of weight? 

It's just... my appetite has been a little off for a few months now. I'll usually just run on coffee through lunch at the office—which I know isn't the best habit, I really should try to eat something—and then by the time I get home, I just kind of pick at dinner with the family. 

But then... I don't know, I guess I've noticed lately that my belt is sitting a notch tighter than it used to. It's probably just my metabolism slowing down a bit in my late thirties, right? I mean, I'm sure it's nothing major. I just need to get back to the gym and I'll drop it in no time. That's pretty common when you're busy with work and family, isn't it?
Are there things that you used to find pleasurable but no longer enjoy at all?

Um... no, not *at all*. I know I just mentioned struggling to get out to the basketball games or the festivals, but I really hope I didn't make it sound like I've just given up on everything. I'd hate for you to think I'm completely checking out of my life, you know? 

There isn't really anything I look at and think, 'I never want to do that again' or that I get absolutely zero pleasure from. I still care about my hobbies and my buddies, I promise. It's really just that the... the enthusiasm is a little dialed back right now because of the stress. But as far as not enjoying something *at all*? No, I don't think I've hit that point. I'm still trying my best to stay engaged with things. That's a good sign, isn't it?
How long have you been feeling less enthusiastic about the things you used to enjoy?

Um... well, it hasn't been forever, I promise. I really don't want to sound like I've just been letting this drag on and on without trying to handle it. I've been doing my best to keep a positive attitude through it all. 

But I guess... if I really think about it... it's probably been around a year and two months? Give or take? That's right around the time the arguments at home started getting a lot worse. It's just been a really stressful patch with my wife, and I think that's just been weighing on me a bit, you know? 

It's completely normal to feel a little less enthusiastic when you're dealing with relationship stuff at home, right? I'm sure once we get things smoothed out, I'll be right back to my old self. I just didn't want to make a big deal out of it and bother anyone. That makes sense, doesn't it?
Have you been feeling sad or empty most of the day, nearly every day?

Um... I wouldn't say I'm completely miserable or crying all the time, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself, because I still go to work and get my job done, and I try to put on a good face for the family. 

But... I guess if I'm being completely honest... yeah, there's been this... this sort of heavy, gray feeling that just kind of tags along with me lately. It's like it follows me from the office, into the car, and then right into the house. And it's weird because even when nothing specific is going wrong, I just feel kind of... hollow? Empty, I guess. 

I mean, I know everyone gets down sometimes, especially with the stress at home I mentioned. It's probably just a normal reaction to being overwhelmed, right? I'm really trying not to let it affect my work or my kids. I just need to push through it and be a bit stronger, don't you think?
Have you been feeling sad or empty for most of the day?

Um, yeah... like I think I was just mentioning a second ago? I hope I didn't explain it poorly before, I definitely don't want to confuse you. But yeah, most days it's just... it's like this heavy, gray mood that just kind of follows me around. From the office, to the car, and right into the house. Even when absolutely nothing specific is happening or going wrong, I just feel kind of hollow. 

But I really am trying not to let it get the best of me, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm just wallowing in it all day. I'm still showing up for work and doing my best, which is the right way to handle it, isn't it? I just hope I'm making sense and giving you the right answers.
For how long have you been feeling less interested in the things you used to enjoy?

Oh, um... I think I might have mentioned this just a little bit ago? I'm so sorry if I wasn't clear enough the first time, I definitely don't want to make you ask things twice. 

But yeah, it's been roughly a year and two months? Give or take a little? It started right around the time the stress and arguments with my wife really picked up. I really hope I'm giving you the right timeline here. I'm trying my best to keep track of it all, but you know how it is when you're just trying to keep your head down and push through for your family. Does that answer it okay for you?
Have you had feelings of worthlessness?

Worthless? Um... well, I wouldn't say *completely* worthless, because I really do try my hardest to provide and do right by them. I don't want you to think I'm a bad father or anything. 

But... I guess, if I'm being open with you... yeah, I do get really down on myself. I hope this doesn't sound too awful, but lately I just keep replaying things in my head. It's like a loop of every late night I stayed at the office, every tailgate I went to when I should have been home, every dumb purchase I've made... 

And I just end up thinking that my wife and kids kind of got stuck with this... this selfish guy who just keeps letting them down. 

I know I shouldn't think that way, and I'm really trying to focus on being better for them, I promise. It's just hard to turn those thoughts off sometimes. That's a pretty normal thing for guys to struggle with, right? I hope I'm not sounding too pathetic saying all that out loud.
For how long have you been having these feelings of being down on yourself and thinking you're letting your family down?

Um... well, it's basically the same timeline as the other things we just talked about. I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture. 

But yeah, it's been about a year and two months. That's when the arguments at home really started getting a lot worse, and I guess that's when those thoughts started creeping in more often. I really do try to brush them off and just focus on being a good provider, though. I know dwelling on it doesn't help anyone. That makes sense, right? I'm just trying to handle it the best way I can.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy but now find no pleasure in at all?

Well, um... I really hope it doesn't sound like I'm just sitting around doing nothing, because I really do try to keep busy and stay active for my family's sake. I know it's important to keep up appearances and, you know, be a fun guy to be around. 

But... yeah, I guess there are a few things. I used to really look forward to playing pickup basketball, or going to bowling nights with the guys... we'd even go to music festivals sometimes, or I'd fire up the smoker in the backyard and have everyone over. 

Lately, though... I don't know, I just kind of end up canceling a lot. Or, if I do go, I'm just sort of... going through the motions, I guess? Like I'm just there so people don't think I'm being a flake. I feel terrible about it, honestly, because I know I should be grateful for those times with friends. I'm really trying to get back into the swing of things, I promise. It's just a phase, right? Like, a lot of guys go through a slump where they just need to focus on work and family instead of hobbies? I hope that's an okay answer.
Have you experienced a loss of interest or pleasure in activities for at least two weeks?

Um, well, like I was saying, it's been going on for a while now. Definitely more than two weeks. I really hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is, because I do still try to show up and be present. I don't want you to think I've just totally given up on everything, you know? I'm still trying my best. But yeah, that feeling of just... not really enjoying those things anymore... it's been pretty constant for over a year now, ever since things got stressful at home. That's pretty typical for this kind of thing, right? I'm just trying to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.
